children: The Investment & Development Conversations session, titled ‘Capital, Confidence & Capacity: Funding India's Hospitality Future’, brought together leaders from hotel development, investment, hospitality businesses and financial institutions to discuss the capital and development landscape shaping India's hospitality future

The 10th edition of the prestigious BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026), hosted at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity, is bringing leading voices from across the hospitality industry for the next two days of conversations on the sector’s growth and evolution. With the theme
‘India’s Hospitality Decade: From Growth to Greatness’
, the Summit will examine the opportunities, challenges and shifts shaping India’s hospitality landscape as the industry enters a defining decade.
‘Capital, Confidence & Capacity: Funding India's Hospitality Future’
, brought together leaders from hotel development, investment, hospitality businesses and financial institutions to discuss the capital and development landscape shaping India's hospitality future.
Rahul Pandit — MD & CEO, Advent Hotels International

Jacob Purackal, Vice President, Development, S Asia, Hilton; Nathan Andrews, Business Head Hospitality & New Projects, DS Group; and Mridul Upreti, Sector Lead - Tourism, Retail & Property, MAS Upstream, Asia Pacific, IFC - International Finance Corporation

Purackal explained, “When you look at the economy to mid-scale market, it’s relatively smaller. In India, franchising is going to become a greater trend. Globally, around 75 per cent of our portfolio is franchised, but in India we are doing what is right for each segment of the market.”

Andrews said, “Our focus will always be on brownfield or operational, first always being operational. The time to market in India is very long. Greenfield projects are like the little white flowers in the bouquet; they are nice to have, but they do not change the numbers dramatically.”

Upreti addressed, “We work hard with the government and Ministry of Tourism. The reason hotels are not being developed in many locations is that there are often issues around space, connectivity and the asset itself. That is the lens through which we look at the opportunity.”

As the discussion drew to a close, speakers highlighted that modern investors expect far more transparency and commercial flexibility from operating partners. By shifting towards collaborative investment frameworks and clearer owner-brand alignment, the industry can unlock institutional capital and accelerate the creation of well-structured hospitality assets.

The two-day BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) encompasses over 25 sessions where hospitality veterans and experts across the nation gathered to provide diverse knowledge and insights. The Summit & Awards is a testament to BW Hotelier’s commitment towards revolutionising Indian hospitality by honouring the crème de la crème of the industry.
